arxiv-2101-09761.creator: B. Quici, N. Hurley-Walker, N. Seymour, R. J. Turner, S. S. Shabala , {}^{\rm\ref{uTAS},\ref{ASTRO3D}}, M. Huynh, H. Andernach, A. D. Kapińska, J. D. arxiv-2101-09761.description: Abstract The remnant phase of a radio galaxy begins when the jets launched from an active galactic nucleus are switched off. To study the fraction of radio galaxies in a remnant phase, we take advantage of a 8.31 8.31 deg 2 sub-region of the GAMA 23 field which comprises of surveys covering the frequency range 0.1–9 GHz.

arxiv-2104-14847.title: Active WeaSuL: Improving Weak Supervision with Active Learning
arxiv-2104-14847.creator: Samantha Biegel, Rafah El-Khatib, Luiz Otavio Vilas Boas Oliveira, Max Baak & Nanne Aben
arxiv-2104-14847.description: Abstract The availability of labelled data is one of the main limitations in machine learning. We can alleviate this using weak supervision: a framework that uses expert-defined rules 𝝀 \bm{\lambda} to estimate probabilistic labels p ⁡ ( y | 𝝀 ) p(y|\bm{\lambda}) for the entire data set.

arxiv-2201-10063.title: Varying Coefficient Model via Adaptive Spline Fitting Thanks: The views expressed herein are the authors alone and are not necessarily the views of Two Sigma Investments, LP, or any of its affiliates.
arxiv-2201-10063.creator: Xufei Wang
arxiv-2201-10063.description: Abstract The varying coefficient model has received broad attention from researchers as it is a powerful dimension reduction tool for non-parametric modeling. Most existing varying coefficient models fitted with polynomial spline assume equidistant knots and take the number of knots as the hyperparameter.

arxiv-2211-13120.title: Frequency space derivation of linear and non-linear memory gravitational wave signals from eccentric binary orbits
arxiv-2211-13120.creator: Arpan Hait, Subhendra Mohanty, Suraj Prakash
arxiv-2211-13120.description: Abstract The memory effect in gravitational wave (GW) signals is the phenomenon, wherein the relative position of two inertial GW detectors undergoes a permanent displacement owing to the passage of GWs through them. Measurement of the memory signal is an important target for future observations as it establishes a connection between observations with field-theoretic results like the soft-graviton theorems.

arxiv-2306-15996.title: Flat bands and magnetism in 𝐅𝐞 𝟒 ​ 𝐆𝐞𝐓𝐞 𝟐 \bm{\mathrm{Fe_{4}GeTe_{2}}} and 𝐅𝐞 𝟓 ​ 𝐆𝐞𝐓𝐞 𝟐 \bm{\mathrm{Fe_{5}GeTe_{2}}} due to bipartite crystal lattices
arxiv-2306-15996.creator: Fuyi Wang, Haijun Zhang ∗
arxiv-2306-15996.description: Abstract Fe n = 4 , 5 ​ GeTe 2 \mathrm{Fe_{n=4,5}GeTe_{2}} exhibits quasi-two-dimensional properties as a promising candidate for a near-room-temperature ferromagnet, which has attracted great interest. In this work, we notice that the crystal lattice of Fe n = 4 , 5 ​ GeTe 2 \mathrm{Fe_{n=4,5}GeTe_{2}} can be approximately regarded as being stacked by three bipartite crystal lattices.

arxiv-2309-13841.title: On the Effectiveness of Adversarial Samples against Ensemble Learning-based Windows PE Malware Detectors Trong-Nghia To, Danh Le Kim, Do Thi Thu Hien, Nghi Hoang Khoa, Hien Do Hoang, Phan The Duy, Van-Hau Pham are with Information Security Lab (InSecLab), University of Information Technology, Vietna
arxiv-2309-13841.creator: Trong-Nghia To 1 2 , Danh Le Kim 1 2 , Do Thi Thu Hien 1 2 , Nghi Hoang Khoa 1 2 , Hien Do Hoang 1 2 , Phan The Duy 1 2 , and Van-Hau Pham 1 2
arxiv-2309-13841.description: Abstract Recently, there has been a growing focus and interest in applying machine learning (ML) to the field of cybersecurity, particularly in malware detection and prevention. Several research works on malware analysis have been proposed, offering promising results for both academic and practical applications.

arxiv-2311-13907.title: Efficient generation of intense spatial and spatiotemporal vortex harmonics using plasma mirrors
arxiv-2311-13907.creator: Yipeng Wu, Zan Nie, Fei Li, Chaojie Zhang, Ken A Marsh, Warren B. Mori, Chan Joshi
arxiv-2311-13907.description: Abstract Intense spatial or spatiotemporal vortex pulses from the extreme ultraviolet to soft X-ray spectral windows are expected to provide new degrees of freedom for a variety of key applications since they carry longitudinal or transverse orbital angular momentum (OAM), respectively.

arxiv-2404-11580.title: Modeling when and how physics PhD students search for a research group: the role of interests and prior research experiences in timely group integration
arxiv-2404-11580.creator: Mike Verostek, Casey W. Miller, Benjamin M. Zwickl
arxiv-2404-11580.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mike Verostek, Casey W. Miller, Benjamin M. Zwickl. Studying the factors that influence the quality of physics PhD students’ doctoral experiences, especially those that motivate them to stay or leave their programs, is critical for providing them with more holistic and equitable support. Prior literature on doctoral attrition has found that students with clear research interests who establish an advisor-advisee relationship early in their graduate careers are most likely to persist.

arxiv-2409-09269.title: Guiding Vision-Language Model Selection for Visual Question-Answering Across Tasks, Domains, and Knowledge Types
arxiv-2409-09269.creator: Neelabh Sinha, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha
arxiv-2409-09269.description: Abstract Visual Question-Answering (VQA) has become key to user experience, particularly after improved generalization capabilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs). But evaluating VLMs for an application requirement using a standardized framework in practical settings is still challenging. This paper aims to solve that using an end-to-end framework.

arxiv-2411-18651.title: Verbalized Representation Learning for Interpretable Few-Shot Generalization
arxiv-2411-18651.creator: Cheng-Fu Yang Da Yin Wenbo Hu Nanyun Peng Bolei Zhou Kai-Wei ChangUniversity of California, Los Angeles cfyang@cs.ucla.edu
arxiv-2411-18651.description: Abstract Humans recognize objects after observing only a few examples, a remarkable capability enabled by their inherent language understanding of the real-world environment. Developing verbalized and interpretable representation can significantly improve model generalization in low-data settings. In this work, we propose Verbalized Representation Learning (VRL), a novel approach for automatically extracting human-interpretable features for object recognition using few-shot data.

arxiv-2412-04792.title: Multi-class heart disease Detection, Classification, and Prediction using Machine Learning Models
arxiv-2412-04792.creator: 1 st Mahfuzul Haque, 2 nd Abu Saleh Musa Miah, 3 rd Debashish Gupta, 4 th Md. Maruf Al Hossain Prince, 5 th Tanzina Alam, 6 th Nusrat Sharmin, 7 th Mohammed Sowket Ali, *8 th Jungpil Shin
arxiv-2412-04792.description: Abstract Heart disease is a leading cause of premature death worldwide, particularly among middle-aged and older adults, with men experiencing a higher prevalence. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), non-communicable diseases, including heart disease, account for 25% (17.9 million) of global deaths, with over 43,204 annual fatalities in Bangladesh.

arxiv-2502-08112.description: Abstract The enigmatic ultraviolet (UV) extinction bump at 2175 Å \,{\rm\AA} , the strongest spectroscopic absorption feature superimposed on the interstellar extinction curve, has recently been detected at the cosmic dawn by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) in JADES-GS-z6-0, a distant galaxy at redshift z ≈ 6.71 z\approx 6.

arxiv-2509-19474.title: Quantum Harmonic Analysis and the Structure in Data: Augmentation
arxiv-2509-19474.creator: Monika Dörfler, Franz Luef, Henry McNulty
arxiv-2509-19474.description: Abstract In this short note, we study the impact of data augmentation on the smoothness of principal components of high-dimensional datasets. Using tools from quantum harmonic analysis, we show that eigenfunctions of operators corresponding to augmented data sets lie in the modulation space M 1 ​ ( ℝ d ) M^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{d}) , guaranteeing smoothness and continuity.

arxiv-2509-20463.title: Efficiently Attacking Memorization Scores
arxiv-2509-20463.creator: Tue Do, Varun Chandrasekaran, Daniel Alabi
arxiv-2509-20463.description: Abstract Influence estimation tools—such as memorization scores—are widely used to understand model behavior, attribute training data, and inform dataset curation. However, recent applications in data valuation and responsible machine learning raise the question: can these scores themselves be adversarially manipulated? In this work, we present a systematic study of the feasibility of attacking memorization-based influence estimators.

arxiv-2511-22813.title: Intelligent Neural Networks: From Layered Architectures to Graph-Organized Intelligence
arxiv-2511-22813.creator: Antoine Salomon
arxiv-2511-22813.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Antoine Salomon. Biological neurons exhibit remarkable intelligence: they maintain internal states, communicate selectively with other neurons, and self-organize into complex graphs rather than rigid hierarchical layers. What if artificial intelligence could emerge from similarly intelligent computational units? We introduce Intelligent Neural Networks (INN) , a paradigm shift where neurons are first-class entities with internal memory and learned communication patterns, organized in complete graphs rather than sequential layers.

arxiv-2601-13237.title: Discover the GLM theory on four pages
arxiv-2601-13237.creator: by V. A. Vladimirov, University of York, vv500@york.ac.uk
arxiv-2601-13237.description: Abstract Abstract The General Lagrangian Mean (GLM) theory uses a version of the averaged equations of fluid dynamics, designed to examine interactions between small-amplitude waves and mean flows. These equations are formulated in coordinates that follow the fluid’s average velocity and are often referred to as ‘pseudo-Lagrangian’ or ‘semi-Lagrangian’.

arxiv-2602-13674.title: An Operator Approach to the Integration of Linear Differential Equations
arxiv-2602-13674.creator: O.V. Kaptsov
arxiv-2602-13674.description: Abstract We develop an operator approach to the integration of linear differential equations based on intertwining relations between differential operators. Conditions for the existence of intertwining operators are obtained, and it is shown that, in low-order cases, the problem reduces to Riccati-type equations. The method is applied to linear partial differential equations, which makes it possible to construct their solutions.

pmc-10628692.title: A new series of acylhydrazones derived from metribuzin with modulated herbicidal activity
pmc-10628692.creator: David Peña, Antonio Lápez-Piñeiro, Damian Fernández, Mark E Light, Juan Manuel Prieto, Lucía Santisteban, Richardo Xhavier Valladares, Pedro Cintas, Reyes Babiano
pmc-10628692.description: This paper reports the preparation and herbicidal evaluation of a small library of acylhydrazones based on the synthetic herbicide metribuzin. The hydrazone linkage easily obtained by reaction of metribuzin with aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes, masks efficiently the exocyclic amino group, thereby altering significantly H-bonding with the receptor and increasing the lipophilicity relative to the parent herbicide.

pmc-11398882.title: Sero-Positive Isolated Ocular Myasthenia Gravis
pmc-11398882.creator: Taimoor A Khan, Muhammad Zeshan Sadiq, Ali A Khan, Muhammad A Zahid, Sheharyar Zameer
pmc-11398882.description: Ocular myasthenia gravis (OMG) is a neuromuscular disease characterized by the production of autoantibodies against post-synaptic proteins at the neuromuscular junction (NMJ). An 18-year-old male who had symptoms of drooping eyelids and double vision was diagnosed with ocular myasthenia gravis on investigations and examinations.

pmc-13239565.title: Using Normalisation Process Theory to Develop a Complex Intervention: A Qualitative Case Study of Screening for Homelessness in Healthcare Settings
pmc-13239565.creator: Nilakshi Gunatillaka, Tze Lin Chai, Suzanne Nielsen, Belinda Hammond, Kimberley Norman, Helen Skouteris, Elizabeth Sturgiss
pmc-13239565.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and AimsNormalisation Process Theory (NPT) seeks to describe and explain how a complex intervention can be embedded into an existing health and social care system. NPT is frequently used to evaluate interventions, and less frequently to design them.We demonstrate how NPT can be applied to exploratory qualitative data to understand the potential barriers and facilitators to the implementation of a new intervention in a health setting using the NPT framework.

pmc-3418594.title: Radiation exposure from CT scans in childhood and subsequent risk of leukaemia and brain tumours: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-3418594.creator: Mark S Pearce, Jane A Salotti, Mark P Little et al.
pmc-3418594.description: Peer-reviewed research article (PubMed Central).
